requirements.title: Permitted science sequences
requirements.summary: Select a two-course/laboratory sequence: PEP 111/112/221; PEP 111 + BIO 181/182; PEP 111 + CH 115/117; CH 115/116/117; CH 115 + BIO 181 + either CH 117 or BIO 182; or CH 115 + PEP 111 + CH 117. Individual titles/credits remain unverified.

requirements.title: Math/science electives
requirements.summary: Choose two 3-credit PEP/CH/BIO/MA courses, excluding required or equivalent coursework; examples of excluded equivalents are MA 117/118/119/134/520. EN 250, CE 240 and NANO 200 may also count. Prior advisor approval required.

requirements.title: Technical electives
requirements.summary: Choose six approved courses: CS 532, 544, 545, CS/CPE 558, CS 560, 582, 584, 589, MA 661, BIA 665, ME 598. Prior advisor approval required; detailed metadata and undergraduate graduate-course access remain unverified.

requirements.title: General electives
requirements.summary: Choose four courses of at least three credits; exclude required/equivalent coursework. Prior advisor approval required.

requirements.title: General elective exclusions
requirements.summary: Excluded: CS 501/515/556/570/573, CS/CPE 590, MA 117/119/134/502. These are restrictions, not an eligible course pool.

requirements.title: Mutually excluded course pairs
requirements.summary: Do not count both: CS 306/396; CS 382 with CS/CPE 550; CS 392/525; CS/CPE 488 with CS/CPE 514; CS/CPE 492 with CS 520; CS 496/510; CS/CPE 442 with CS 561; SSW 540 with CS 347; CS 346/546.

requirements.title: Humanities requirements
requirements.summary: Program requirements defer to a linked university Humanities Requirements policy, which remains unreviewed.

requirements.title: SUCCESS required course
requirements.summary: All students complete PRV 101. Its credit value is observed in the academic plan.

requirements.title: SUCCESS course selection
requirements.summary: Complete three of PRV 201, PRV 202, PRV 203, PRV 204 or PRV 205. Individual titles and credits remain unverified.

requirements.title: Undergraduate access to graduate courses
requirements.summary: For 500-level courses, undergraduates need junior standing and the course prerequisites; enroll in an A-U section or request an eligibility override, subject to academic review and instructor/Graduate Academics approval. The separate rule for 600+ SES/SSB courses requires fifth-semester standing, GPA 3.25, permission and no more than two per semester. The latter explicitly names SES/SSB; its applicability to School of Computing is not assumed.

requirements.title: External-course approval
requirements.summary: While enrolled, request transfer approval before external registration and submit an official transcript; C or better is required. Outside grades do not affect Stevens GPA, even for previously attempted Stevens courses. Full-time Stevens students (12–18 credits) cannot simultaneously take external courses. At most two U.S. humanities courses may transfer while enrolled; upper-level humanities must come from four-year institutions.

requirements.title: University graduation and residency
requirements.summary: Pass required major courses, earn cumulative GPA 2.00 and at least 1.75 across senior-year courses. At least 50 percent of required graduation credits must be completed at Stevens; the transfer policy separately caps transferred credit at 50 percent.

requirements.title: AI humanities distribution
requirements.summary: All undergraduates take HASS 103 and HASS 105. The School of Computing AI row then requires one humanities course, one social science or science-and-technology-studies course, one course from any of those groups, and one of HST 381/HSSC 371/HPL 455. This clarifies the existing plan slots rather than adding duplicate courses. HQSS 300 does not qualify; ECON 243/244 qualify only if not required in the major. The lower language/music/theater/art approval list is explicitly labeled SES/Business, so its applicability to Computing remains unresolved.

requirements.title: Elected pass/fail restrictions
requirements.summary: Pass/fail requires Dean’s List or cumulative GPA 3.50, advisor approval and an extra undergraduate course beyond degree requirements; at most one such course per semester. Graduate courses cannot use pass/fail. Audited courses earn no credit.

requirements.title: Incoming advanced/transfer credit
requirements.summary: Incoming first-year students may receive up to 30 credits from approved AP/IB/A-Level exams or college courses in high school. Transfer students submit prior courses and syllabi for evaluation and construct an academic plan with their advisor; no more than 50 percent of graduation credits may transfer.
